#  Examine relationships between predictors and house price
## Identify numeric variables and descriptive analysis
```{R}
num_vars <- names(df)[sapply(df, is.numeric)]

desc_stats <- df %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(num_vars),
                   list(
                     n     = ~ sum(!is.na(.)),
                     mean  = ~ mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
                     sd    = ~ sd(.,   na.rm = TRUE),
                     min   = ~ min(.,  na.rm = TRUE),
                     q25   = ~ quantile(., 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
                     med   = ~ median(., na.rm = TRUE),
                     q75   = ~ quantile(., 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
                     max   = ~ max(.,  na.rm = TRUE)
                   ))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to  = c("variable", "stat"),
    names_sep = "_(?=[^_]+$)"   # split at the LAST underscore
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = stat, values_from = value) %>%
  arrange(variable)

print(desc_stats)
```

# Correlation among numeric predictors
```{r}
cor_num <- cor(df[, num_vars], use = "complete.obs")
print(round(cor_num, 2))

# Correlation of numeric predictors with target
cor_target <- cor(
  df[, num_vars],
  df$House_Price_Million_KES,
  use = "complete.obs"
)
# Melt the correlation matrix into long format
cor_melt <- melt(cor_num)
colnames(cor_melt) <- c("Var1", "Var2", "Correlation")

# Heatmap
ggplot(cor_melt, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = Correlation)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Correlation, 2)), size = 3, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#B2182B", mid = "white", high = "#2166AC",
    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1),
    name = "Pearson\nr"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation Heatmap of Numeric Predictors",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  ) +
  coord_fixed()
```

#  Convert categorical variables into numerical representations
```{r}
df_model <- df %>% select(-House_ID)

dummies <- dummyVars(House_Price_Million_KES ~ ., data = df_model)
df_encoded <- predict(dummies, newdata = df_model) %>% as.data.frame()
df_encoded$House_Price_Million_KES <- df_model$House_Price_Million_KES
str(df_encoded)

```


#  Divide data into training and testing sets
```{r}
set.seed(123)
train_index <- createDataPartition(
  df_encoded$House_Price_Million_KES,
  p = 0.8,
  list = FALSE
)

train <- df_encoded[train_index, ]
test  <- df_encoded[-train_index, ]

cat("Train rows:", nrow(train), " Test rows:", nrow(test), "\n")
```


#  Build Random Forest Regression model
```{r}
set.seed(123)  # for reproducibility
rf_model <- randomForest(
  House_Price_Million_KES ~ .,
  data = train,
  ntree = 500,
  mtry = 3,
  importance = TRUE
)

print(rf_model)

```

#   predictions for test data
```{r}
pred <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test)
head(pred)
```

# Evaluate model: RMSE, MAE, R2, MAPE
```{r}
actual <- test$House_Price_Million_KES

rmse <- sqrt(mean((actual - pred)^2))
mae  <- mean(abs(actual - pred))
r2   <- 1 - sum((actual - pred)^2) / sum((actual - mean(actual))^2)
mape <- mean(abs((actual - pred) / actual)) * 100

metrics <- c(
  RMSE = rmse,
  MAE = mae,
  R2 = r2,
  MAPE = mape
)

print(round(metrics, 3))

```

#  Compare actual and predicted house prices
```{r}
comparison <- data.frame(
  Actual = actual,
  Predicted = pred,
  Residual = actual - pred
)

head(comparison)
write.csv(comparison, "actual_vs_predicted.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

#  Plot Actual vs Predicted values
```{r}
ggplot(comparison, aes(x = Actual, y = Predicted)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0,
    slope = 1,
    color = "red",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Actual vs Predicted House Prices",
    x = "Actual Price (Million KES)",
    y = "Predicted Price (Million KES)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

#  Examine variable importance
```{r}
imp <- importance(rf_model)
print(imp[order(imp[, "%IncMSE"], decreasing = TRUE), ])
varImpPlot(rf_model, main = "Variable Importance")
```

# 18. The most important predictors
- The most important predictors are LocationRunda, House_Size_m2, and ConditionFair, which lead on both %IncMSE (34.6, 27.6, 27.3) and IncNodePurity (13,437; 38,729; 12,368), indicating they drive both predictive accuracy and node splits. They are closely followed by LocationKitengela, ConditionExcellent, Bedrooms, and Bathrooms (all with %IncMSE above 20), showing that location, size, condition, and room count dominate house price variation. Mid-tier predictors include ConditionGood, LocationKileleshwa, LocationKilimani, House_Age_Years, and Distance_CBD_km (%IncMSE ~14–18), while Plot_Size_m2 and LocationSyokimau contribute modestly. The least important predictors are Has_Garden (both levels), LocationRoysambu, LocationRuaka, and Parking_Spaces (%IncMSE < 7), suggesting they add little unique information once location, size, and condition are accounted for.
